$comment: Normalization for compare-records.py (design-decisions D7 item 2, D14.6, D14.23).
volatileKeyNames/volatileKeySuffixes replace a value with <volatile> in the STRUCTURAL column,
so a run-to-run clock is never reported as a contract change. They only see string values: the
numeric twins of these keys (ticks, *Ticks, *Us, wallSeconds) are numbers and are therefore
governed by the per-key jitter band in column 3, never by this list.
pathKeyNames replace the absolute paths with <path>. Nothing else is path-like: run.json's
arms[].file is a bare file name and keeps its literal value, so the arm-to-file mapping is
compared too (a renamed arm file shows up as a group present on one side only).
endpointKeyNames keep the address of an endpoint and normalize only its port. A ledger peer is
the client's source address plus the OS-chosen ephemeral port: the port changes every run and is
never a contract value, while a changed address still has to be reported.
numericTextKeyNames rewrites only the interpolated DECIMAL measurements inside prose notes (the
F3 rates and F1 ceilings such as 40.191 requests/s or 203826.7 ms, which move every run), so the
note template is still compared; whole-number constants quoted in a note (the 256/16384 deferred
queue bound, 4096 in-flight window, 1048576 cap, RFC numbers) stay compared as literals.
conditionalPathPatterns list the paths a well-formed run may publish on one side only
(a pure-TCP or pure-UDP arm omits the other family's block; an empty histogram is omitted),
they are reported in column 2 and never fail the comparison.
volatileArityPatterns list arrays whose element count is data-dependent.
